hints: Set up horizontal and vertical axes and resolve all three coplanar forces into perpendicular components.
Apply the equilibrium condition by equating the sum of the components in each direction to zero: $X \cos \theta - 40 = 0$ and $X \sin \theta - 30 = 0$.
Divide the vertical equation by the horizontal equation to find $\tan \theta$, then square and add both equations to find $X$.
walkthrough: When a system of coplanar forces is in equilibrium, the resultant force along any direction must be zero. We define the horizontal direction to the right as positive $x$ and the vertical direction upwards as positive $y$:

Resolve forces along the horizontal axis ($x$-direction). The force of magnitude $X$ has component $+X \cos \theta$, the $40\text{ N}$ force acts purely to the left ($-40\text{ N}$), and the $30\text{ N}$ force has no horizontal component:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies X \cos \theta - 40 = 0 \implies X \cos \theta = 40$$

Resolve forces along the vertical axis ($y$-direction). The force of magnitude $X$ has component $+X \sin \theta$, the $30\text{ N}$ force acts downwards ($-30\text{ N}$), and the $40\text{ N}$ force has no vertical component:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies X \sin \theta - 30 = 0 \implies X \sin \theta = 30$$

To find the angle $\theta$, eliminate $X$ by dividing the vertical equation by the horizontal equation:
$$\frac{X \sin \theta}{X \cos \theta} = \frac{30}{40}$$
$$\tan \theta = \frac{3}{4} = 0.75$$

Take the inverse tangent to find $\theta$:
$$\theta = \arctan(0.75) = 36.8698^\circ \approx 36.9^\circ$$

To find $X$, square both component equations and add them together, using the identity $\cos^2 \theta + \sin^2 \theta = 1$:
$$(X \cos \theta)^2 + (X \sin \theta)^2 = 40^2 + 30^2$$
$$X^2 (\cos^2 \theta + \sin^2 \theta) = 1600 + 900$$
$$X^2 (1) = 2500$$
$$X = \sqrt{2500} = 50$$
